library_preparation_preflight.agent_guidance: This is a pure API bundle with no service, so no Docker image or system properties are needed. It has 4 classes: ProxyManager, InvocationHandlerWrapper, UnableToProxyException and FinalModifierException. Write tests that implement ProxyManager and InvocationHandlerWrapper in test code. A simple implementation backed by java.lang.reflect.Proxy works; pass a null Bundle, since the tests run outside an OSGi framework. Exercise FinalModifierException.getMessage() for both a final class (the (Class) constructor) and final methods (the (Class, String) constructor). This is the main dynamic-access path: outside OSGi, FrameworkUtil.getBundle returns null, so MessageUtil falls back to ResourceBundle.getBundle("org.apache.aries.proxy.nls.ProxyMessages"). That needs resource-bundle metadata for org/apache/aries/proxy/nls/ProxyMessages.properties in native image. Also cover the UnableToProxyException constructors and getClassName().
risks: MessageUtil.createMessageUtil(Class, String) binds the ResourceBundle with the default locale. If generated tests assert exact message text, they should pin Locale.ROOT or Locale.ENGLISH.

There is very little code to cover: 4 classes, 2 of them interfaces. The only real dynamic access is the ProxyMessages resource bundle lookup in aries.util. Dynamic-access coverage will be small, and most of it falls in the org.apache.aries.util.nls package.
